brand_within_channel: Prime Documentary constitutional-rights style applied to the car-search / automobile-exception episode: dark-noir, cinematic, faceless, explanatory; the concept itself moves (Kurzgesagt/TED-Ed-grade motion graphics) over a Veritasium-grade b-roll bed. Not stock-plus-text.

dissent_only: muted matte red #C0473E (VoteTally dissent seat only)

mood: present-tense unease (the stop) into legal clarity (the rule), a rising turn (the driveway), a hard payoff (the line slams down), then a calm, resolved throughline.
lighting: low-key, high-contrast, controlled practical light, volumetric haze, fine film grain; night/blue-hour dominant; 1920s beats add warm brass/amber; every frame crop-safe with negative space for kinetic type.
people_rule: No identifiable likeness of George Carroll, Chief Justice Taft, Justice McReynolds, Ryan Collins, Justice Sotomayor, Justice Alito, or any modern person. Collins is a living person (R2): role only, never a face. Use POV, hands, backs, torsos, silhouettes, distance, and diagrams. No deepfake or portrait reconstruction.
disclosure_rule: All AI reenactment/location/object stills are symbolic reconstruction; a small on-screen label appears at least once per reenactment sequence, and every selected still is rights-registered before edit use. Reconstructions are never presented as authentic archival footage (invariant 11).

hero_motif.name: THE BRIGHT LINE
hero_motif.spec: A glowing electric-blue seam of light running along the ground between a car silhouette (left) and a house silhouette (right). mode=draw seeds it in the hook; mode=hold breathes through the acts; mode=slam is the single hardest hit in the film — the Court said NO (Collins), the hook paid off, Trail motion blur + a decaying white flash. Rendered in Remotion so text/standards are exact.
hero_motif.render: carsearch/BrightLine.tsx — motion graphic, not AI-image text.

typography.case_cards: Display weight, large gold/electric-blue on black/navy; kinetic mask-cut-up entrances with motion blur.
typography.citation_lower_thirds: Small caps, silver with gold case/claim accent; exact citations and votes rendered in Remotion (Carroll 1925, Gant 2009, Collins 2018 8-1).
typography.open_captions: Burned-in later, high contrast, bottom third, per channel style.
typography.generated_image_text_policy: No text inside AI stills. All words, dates, counters, votes, quotes, citations and labels are Remotion overlays.

continuity_strategy: Codex generates the 40 hero stills (S001-S040) first; local commercial-OK SDXL/SD3.5 only for owner-approved fixes or emergency gap-fills (rule 19). Single style family: cinematic symbolic noir, faceless people, 16:9, dark navy + electric-blue + gold. >=40% of still cuts receive DepthStill parallax (depth maps pre-generated by gen_depth.py); the rest get Ken Burns. Factory b-roll (~100+ clips) is contact-sheet eyeballed before staging (labels are known-corrupt). 3-4 candidates for Tier A stills, 2-3 for Tier B, then QC.

thumbnail_concept.primary: Night car with an open trunk and a bright electric-blue line slamming across the ground toward a house, bold hook: 'CAN THEY SEARCH YOUR CAR?' or 'ONE LINE THEY CAN'T CROSS'.
alts: the bright line between a car and a house with 'IT STOPS AT YOUR HOME'
car-key turning in a house door with 'A KEY TO YOUR HOME?'

do_not: rewrite or visually contradict the approved script
present symbolic visuals as authentic footage (invariant 11)
show Carroll, Taft, McReynolds, Collins, Sotomayor, or Alito as identifiable people
state Collins 7-1 (it is 8-1) or misattribute the majority/dissent
use the banned WipeTransition gold vertical sweep or default crossfades
leave any still frozen — every still gets DepthStill parallax or Ken Burns
use generated images for exact legal text, votes, or quotes
let corrupted factory-shelf labels inject off-theme footage (cowboy/cartoon) — eyeball every clip
